title: Detection of inert cocartesian edges by target color projections
statement: Use the universes, coherent triangles and quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity categories and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a monoidal infinity category. Let $u:x\to y$ lie over an inert map $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$, where $s,r\geq0$. For each $1\leq i\leq r$, choose a $p$-cocartesian edge $t_i:y\to y_i$ over the consecutive-edge projection $\rho_i:[r]\to[1]$, and a coherent triangle with short edges $u,t_i$ and long edge $w_i:x\to y_i$ over $\rho_i\alpha$. Then $u$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if every $w_i$ is $p$-cocartesian. This holds for every choice of the projections and triangles. For $r=0$ the condition is empty, so every edge over an inert map to $[0]$ is $p$-cocartesian. No cocartesianness of $u$ is assumed when choosing its target color projections, and no colimits are required.
